coupling: The defect is a semantic conflict over the meaning of the local variable 'eo' in pcre2_regexec() between two consecutive real maintenance commits, both in src/pcre2posix.c. Commit abbf691 (#1022, 'do not truncate the subject length to int') is edited to normalize eo to hold the subject LENGTH: it sets eo = rm_eo - rm_so in the REG_STARTEND branch and passes eo directly to pcre2_match() instead of (eo - so). Read alone this is complete, correct, and self-consistent: so holds the start offset, eo the length, and (string + so, eo) is exactly the declared subject. Commit 2d3a98a (#1009, 'validate REG_STARTEND offsets') is edited so that, while adding its real NULL/offset validation, it also assigns eo = (PCRE2_SIZE)pmatch[0].rm_eo (the ABSOLUTE end offset, upstream text) without updating the pcre2_match() call site changed by the previous commit. Read alone this also looks correct: in upstream code eo IS the absolute end and (eo - so) at the call site is the length. Only when the two commits compose does pcre2_match() get called as (string + so, eo) with eo = absolute rm_eo: for any REG_STARTEND call with rm_so > 0 the declared subject length over-runs the real buffer by rm_so bytes, and the matcher reads past the end of the caller's allocation (ASan heap-buffer-overflow in match() at pcre2_match.c:1732). The fix is necessarily non-local: reverting either edited commit's diff alone removes the bug (reverting #1022's edit restores (eo - so) with absolute eo; reverting #1009's edit restores eo = rm_eo - rm_so with the direct eo argument), but each single-commit 'fix' contradicts the other commit's convention, so a reviewer must reason across both commits - agreeing one convention for so/eo and using it consistently at both the assignment and the call site - to repair it correctly.
